title: Speaking practice rubric
provenance: Written by EduWonderLab for classroom practice. Informed by the kinds of features WIDA describes (discourse, sentence and word/phrase level) but it is NOT a WIDA rubric, uses none of its wording, and produces no WIDA score or level.

dimensions.label: Task fulfillment
dimensions.look: Did the response do what the prompt asked, for the purpose and audience given?
descriptors: Little of what the prompt asked is addressed.
Part of the task is addressed; something important is missing.
The main parts of the task are addressed.
The whole task is addressed, with its purpose and audience clear.

dimensions.label: Organization and coherence
dimensions.look: Do the ideas come in an order a listener can follow?
descriptors: Ideas are hard to follow.
Some ideas are in order; others are scattered.
Ideas follow a clear order, with some connecting words.
Ideas build in a clear order and are connected throughout.

dimensions.label: Vocabulary appropriateness
dimensions.look: Are the words right for the topic and the listener?
descriptors: Few topic words are used.
Some topic words are used; some are unclear or repeated.
Topic words are used and mostly fit the meaning.
Precise topic and academic words are used to say exactly what is meant.

dimensions.label: Sentence-level language
dimensions.look: Are the sentences complete enough to carry the meaning?
descriptors: Mostly single words or fragments.
Some complete sentences; meaning is sometimes lost.
Complete sentences carry the meaning, with some variety.
A variety of sentence types carries the meaning smoothly.

dimensions.label: Elaboration
dimensions.look: Are there details, reasons or examples, not only a statement?
descriptors: Statements only.
One detail or reason is given.
Details, reasons or examples support the main points.
Specific, well-chosen details, reasons or evidence support every main point.

dimensions.label: Clarity of communication
dimensions.look: Could a listener understand the message?
descriptors: The message is very hard to understand.
The message is understood with effort.
The message is understood.
The message is easy to understand.

dimensions.label: Use of academic language
dimensions.look: Does the response use language typical of the subject (for example, words that explain, compare or justify)?
descriptors: Everyday words only.
A few subject words or linking words appear.
Subject words and linking words are used appropriately.
Subject words and linking words are used accurately and with control.

notScoredNote: These are judged by a person listening. The lab never infers them from how long or how loud a recording is, and it runs no speech analysis.
